ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, subscriber, authorized signatory, and UBO against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated list and Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (ii) FINTRAC's politically exposed person framework, covering foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and Heads of International Organizations; (iii) FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction lists; and (iv) OFAC's SDN list on a best-efforts basis where USD clearing, US counterparties, or US nexus exists. Enhanced due diligence requires source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and a FINTRAC suspicious transaction report where any red flag is triggered. This entity is classified as Low_Risk_Standard for AML purposes; the incorporating firm must nonetheless document all screening results and retain records for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta); filings submitted electronically through Authorized Registry Agents; name search via the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system at www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French (or a Roman-character transliteration of a foreign name) and must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC' or 'U.L.C.'. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing corporate names, extra-provincial registrations, and registered trademarks under ABCA s 10(5) and the Alberta Name Regulation; a NUANS report dated within 90 days before filing must accompany the articles of incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss. 6 (incorporation), 10 (articles of incorporation), 15.1 (unlimited liability corporation election), 101 (registered office), 106-108 (directors), 125 (officers), together with the regulations under the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta); online portal: Corporate Registry Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation (including designation of Unlimited Liability Corporation status, registered office, first directors, and share structure); filing fee CAD 50.00 (≈ USD 37.00)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; the Corporation may issue common shares without par value for such consideration as the directors determine; no mandatory escrow or capital deposit is required by the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] UNLIMITED LIABILITY CORPORATION: 1. The initial directors constitute the first board. 2. The issuance of 100 common shares without par value to the founding shareholder for CAD 100.00 is approved; the President is directed to deposit the subscription funds, issue share certificates, and maintain the share register. 3. The registered office is fixed at [address], Alberta, which is also the records office. 4. Officers are appointed: President, Corporate Secretary, and Treasurer. 5. The by-laws and corporate seal are adopted. 6. The President and Secretary may execute all filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via a NUANS-authorized search house (Corporate Registry Service online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed name containing the mandatory 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' suffix (ABCA s. 15.1). Review the Name Search Report for confusing similarity with existing Alberta or federal names. Reserve the cleared name; the report remains valid for 90 days from the search date.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS Name Search Request form
NUANS search fee (CAD 21.00)
Proposed corporate name and two alternate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or refused for confusing similarity, obtain a fresh NUANS report for an alternate name and revise the name field in the Articles of Incorporation before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) with ULC Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registry Service online filing portal (Registrar of Corporations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and attest Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation online, inserting the reserved name, the unlimited liability corporation election under ABCA s. 15.1, the Alberta registered office address, the class structure of common shares without par value, and full particulars of the first directors with their signed consents. Pay the CAD 50.00 filing fee through the secure portal; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Corporate Access Number (CAN) upon approval.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report (less than 90 days old)
Completed Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation
Consent of first directors (included in Form 1)
Identification of incorporator (name and Alberta service address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice or correction request (e.g., invalid name or incomplete director consents), correct and resubmit the Form 1 within 30 days; no second incorporation fee is charged for a Registrar-generated correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Actions, Share Subscription, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate records officer / first board of directors (internal corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Certificate of Incorporation in the corporate minute book, execute the first board resolutions, issue common shares against the founding shareholder's subscription of CAD 100.00, and establish the share register, corporate seal, and approved by-laws. Retain all statutory records, including the register of directors and registered office records, at the Alberta registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and CAN
Executed first board resolutions and by-laws
Share subscription agreement and paid subscription funds
Minute book, share register, register of directors, and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscriber fails to pay the subscribed amount, the board may serve a written call for payment and, upon continued default, cancel the relevant shares and reset the share register without prejudice to the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the CAN and Certificate of Incorporation, register the Corporation with the CRA to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN), the federal corporate income tax account (RC), the GST/HST account (RT) for Canadian retail supplies, a payroll (RP) account if employees are engaged, and an import/export account should cross-border shipments require customs entry. Complete the CRA registration questionnaire; ULC shareholders may subsequently file check-the-box elections with the IRS to treat the entity as a disregarded or partnership entity for U.S. tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation / Corporate Access Number
First board resolution listing authorized representatives for tax filings
Director identification and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA validation flags a mismatch with the corporate registry, provide the verified CAN confirmation and a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation via the CRA business verification window, or call the Business Enquiries line (1-800-959-5525) to release the accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority of the city/town where any office, warehouse, or trade premises is located (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licensing or City of Edmonton Licence & Permit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the Corporation maintains a physical warehouse or office in Alberta for the fulfilment of internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment, apply for a non-residential municipal Business Licence; confirm the premises satisfies the Alberta Building Code 2019 and Alberta Fire Code requirements, arrange an inspection, and pay the applicable municipal licence fee before commencing occupancy.
required_dossiers: Municipal Business Licence application
Lease or proof of premises ownership
Fire and building inspection reports
WCB-Alberta registration confirmation (workers' compensation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality imposes conditions or withholds the licence due to fire or occupancy deficiencies, remedy the identified defects, obtain a re-inspection and a certificate of occupancy, and resubmit the corrected application without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Alberta Annual Return and Continuing Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations) and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Alberta Annual Return electronically within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary (fee CAD 25.00) and update the registered office and directors records maintained in the corporate registry. Prepare and file the T2 corporate income tax return within six months of the fiscal year-end, remit GST/HST as applicable, and retain board resolutions covering any changes to officers, registered office, or share capital.
required_dossiers: Alberta Annual Return Form (online template)
Updated register of directors and registered office record
T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and financial statements
GST/HST remittance schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporation is struck off for two consecutive unfiled annual returns, apply for reinstatement with the Registrar under ABCA s. 222, file all delinquent returns, pay the reinstatement fee, and resume statutory compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — e-commerce retail warehousing and non-destructive storage of camping equipment are not designated activities under the EPEA Activities Designation Regulation (AR 276/2003); no environmental impact assessment, registration, or approval applies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; packaging and recyclable material is segregated and disposed of under the Alberta Recycling Regulation (AR 99/2004) and municipal solid-waste by-laws; any sanitary discharge is limited to municipal sewer connections under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26, and stored fuels or propane canisters in retail inventory comply with the Alberta Fire Code storage limits

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection of warehouse premises under the Alberta Building Code 2019 and Alberta Fire Code 2019; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and OHS Code (AR 87/2009); WCB-Alberta workers' compensation account; racking and forklift safety inspections where warehousing is performed

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) — Business Registration Online portal; provincial income tax administered under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement; CBSA for import/export accounts

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); exchange-rate policy authority formally rests with the Minister of Finance / Department of Finance Canada; prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions is administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border AML/CTF transaction reporting is administered by FINTRAC. Canada has no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration because the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account. Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and imposes no exchange-control restrictions on payments or transfers for current international transactions or on capital flows. There are no statutory approvals for profit remittances (dividends, interest, royalties, management fees) or for capital repatriation by a non-resident shareholder. The practical hurdles are tax-driven, not exchange-control-driven: (i) Part XIII withholding tax of 25% on deemed dividends, interest, and royalties paid by the ULC to non-residents, reduced to 15% (or 5% for direct-dividend shareholders) and 0% on arm's-length interest under the Canada-US Treaty, subject to limitation-on-benefits and special ULC hybrid-mismatch rules under Treaty Article IV(7); (ii) E-commerce GST/HST registration and collection obligations on Canadian sales; and (iii) reporting obligations to Statistics Canada through the International Transactions Reporting System and to FINTRAC for wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000. An Alberta ULC with a US shareholder that has made a check-the-box election may present treaty-mismatch complexity that Canadian tax counsel must document before the first dividend distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio; Canadian exporters may hold foreign currency indefinitely in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts. The binding statutory obligations are: (i) CBSA export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for every export shipment with a value exceeding CAD 2,000, filed at the time of export for sea, air, and road modes, and within 15 calendar days after the date of exportation for goods shipped by mail or courier; (ii) FINTRAC Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Report (CCMIR) for physical import or export of currency or monetary instruments equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000; and (iii) for income-tax purposes, export receipts must be translated into CAD at a reasonable exchange rate (Bank of Canada daily rate or noon rate) on the relevant taxation date, and accrued foreign-exchange gains are taxable on income account for an e-commerce retailer. No central-bank approval is required to receive, hold, or disburse foreign-currency trade proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low; legally constrained. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK electronic money institution (EMI) licence, and the Bank Act restricts deposit-taking and payment-system clearing to licensed banks (Schedule I/II) and regulated credit unions. An offshore fintech EMI cannot hold CAD deposits for an Alberta ULC or settle through Payments Canada rails (Lynx, Real-Time Rail). The ULC may use an offshore EMI only as a supplementary card-acquiring and payouts gateway, provided the EMI obtains FINTRAC foreign money-services-business (FMSB) registration where applicable and its services do not constitute deposit-taking in Canada. Core treasury clearing, FX execution, and corporate credit must remain hosted by a Schedule I Canadian bank; Stripe and PayPal are acceptable only as front-end settlement rails that finally settle into the Schedule I operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an Alberta ULC with non-resident shareholders, Schedule I banks generally require physical attendance of at least one director or authorized signatory at a Canadian branch for the initial corporate account opening, or a video-KYC interview conducted through the bank's international private-banking desk. Remote opening without in-branch attendance is possible only where the director is Canadian-resident and the bank accepts dual-process identity verification (for example, credit-file validation plus government-issued identity evidence) or notarized identification presented through a bank-approved intermediary. The ULC must deliver a certified copy of the Alberta Certificate of Status, certified corporate registers, a board resolution or unanimous-shareholder agreement naming signatories, and a shareholder acknowledgment accepting the unlimited-liability feature. A substantive beneficial-ownership interview should be expected, covering source of wealth, expected turnover, payment-acceptance mix (Stripe and PayPal), supplier jurisdictions, and confirmation that business receipts do not include cryptocurrency settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration in an unlimited-liability vehicle: a single US person or US parent holding 100% of the Alberta ULC may be treated as enhanced-risk complex ownership and trigger source-of-wealth requests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Certificate of Status; certified shareholder register and unanimous shareholder agreement; IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election record or explicit abandoned-election statement; IRS Form W-9 or W-8BEN-E for the ULC and ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth report from the shareholder's depository bank; board resolution approving account opening; Canadian legal opinion confirming ULC validity, good standing, and signatory capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-velocity anomaly: repeated daily deposits from Stripe and PayPal with card-not-present retail descriptors, no single payer identifiers, and elevated refund or chargeback ratios, suggesting possible layering rather than genuine e-commerce.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements; six months of PSP settlement reports; order-level transaction logs; chargeback and refund analytics; website domain and operating-address verification; GST/HST registration certificate; supplier purchase invoices and 3PL warehouse contracts corroborating physical outdoor-gear inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering screen: disbursements to manufacturers in the PRC or Southeast Asia in which invoice values, bill-of-lading weights, and customs declarations are inconsistent, or where supplier bank accounts are held in third-party jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders; pro-forma invoices; final commercial invoices; bills of lading or airway bills; CERS export declarations where goods are re-exported; CBSA customs entries; third-party inspection certificates (SGS, Bureau Veritas); supplier corporate-registration and KYB pack; transfer-pricing memorandum for any related-party supplier; confirmation from Canadian trade counsel that no over- or under-invoicing exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital-escrow credit from a foreign private bank or offshore jurisdiction with opaque remitter naming (for example, a holding company with no disclosed business) and no supporting contract, creating an unexplained-third-party-funds flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 copy; bank-to-bank remitter reference; executed share-subscription agreement; board minutes authorizing the share issue; source-of-funds attestation supported by remitter account statements; organizational chart showing the direct matching entity; independent counsel opinion confirming that the remitter is the true registered shareholder and that no undisclosed third-party funds are interposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – online via CorpReg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50; failure to file for 2 consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off/dissolution under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (taxation year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; interest charged on outstanding balances; repeated failure may lead to criminal prosecution and personal director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A non-distributing private corporation (including a ULC) is exempt from mandatory independent audit; an audit becomes compulsory if the corporation is a distributing corporation, if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand one, or if articles/by-laws require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) – Part II of CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS permitted for all corporations but mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and the Canada Business Corporations Act (if applicable), the register of individuals with significant control (ISC) must be kept updated, and the annual return must include a confirmation that such register is accurate and complete. There is no separate 'annual confirmation' document; however, any change in significant control, including share transfers, must be recorded in the ISC register within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500–15,000 (if audit required; otherwise not applicable)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income from active business carried on in Canada
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must report income attributable to Canadian sources or business carried on in Canada
For non-residents, include worldwide income if business in Canada

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $100 per day up to a maximum of $2,500, plus interest on unpaid taxes and potential gross negligence penalties

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and submit a Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to the CRA to claim reduced withholding tax rates under applicable double tax agreements
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% federal rate, reduced under treaties (e.g., 0-5% for US); Interest: 25% federal rate, reduced under treaties (e.g., 0% for portfolio interest)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory documentation filing threshold; recommended for related party transactions exceeding $1 million in value
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities engaged in relevant activities; ULC in Alberta may require compliance if carrying on qualifying activities such as holding intellectual property

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late or non-submission of T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of $100 per day, capped at $2,500, plus interest and possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for penalties and potential imprisonment for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to apply arm's length principles or maintain required transfer pricing documentation for related party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, penalties up to 10% of the transaction value, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Potential personal liability including fines and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold, collect, or remit withholding tax on dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax, plus interest, and possible criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for the tax and penalties; possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a ULC as a shell entity without genuine economic substance or to evade taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, penalties, and potential criminal charges under the Income Tax Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment for up to 2 years, substantial fines, and director disqualification
